text.p: Nextel Communications Inc said on Thursday that it expected operating losses for the next two and a half years, but despite investing $1.2 billion over that time did not expect to come to the market for more funds.
"Over the next 2-1/2 years we will invest another $1.2 billion or so in capital equipment," chief financial officer Steven Shindler told an investment conference.
"Operating losses will consist of another $400 million to $500 million over that time," he said.
Shindler saw no need to tap the debt or equity markets.

"Between our new bank financing committments we have from a number of vendors and cash we have on our balance sheet we forecast we have enough to carry us through the spills in that timeframe," he said.
Nextel's annual report shows $409 million of cash and marketable securities at end-1995.

He said that proceeds would come through from Comcast Corp, which originally got its Nextel stake as part of Nextel's 1995 purchase of DialPage, and from billionaire wireless entrepreneur Craig McCaw.
McCaw and his family invested an initial $315 million in Nextel in April 1995, but options could take that up to a total of $1.1 billion.
Wireless services company Nextel is aiming for a specialist market, providing push-to-talk phones for mobile workers in airports, hotels and in security. -- New York Newsroom 212 859 1610
